takeaway: Olfactory nerve fibres pass through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone. A fracture here can damage the olfactory bulbs, causing anosmia and cerebrospinal rhinorrhoea.

lines.text: A thirty-year-old man was in a road traffic accident.
He fractured his anterior cranial fossa.
At that time, he had cerebrospinal rhinorrhoea.
Five weeks later, he presents with anosmia: he cannot smell.
Olfactory nerve fibres pass through the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone.
A fracture here can damage the olfactory bulbs,
and that causes both anosmia and cerebrospinal rhinorrhoea.
So the fractured bone behind his anosmia is the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone.
